title: CLI --repeat N prints the greeting N times; N < 1 is a usage error
spec: main(argv) in src/samplecli/cli.py treats argv[0] as the name, so main(['--repeat', '3', 'Ada']) prints 'Hello, --repeat!'. Add a --repeat N option (N an integer, default 1) that prints the greeting line N times, one per line. The option may appear before or after the optional positional name: main(['--repeat', '3', 'Ada']) and main(['Ada', '--repeat', '3']) both print 'Hello, Ada!\n' three times and return 0. The existing name handling (greet-003, greet-005) is unchanged and applies to every repetition: ends stripped, internal whitespace runs collapsed to one space, blank or missing name becomes 'world'. Without --repeat the output is exactly one line, as today. N of 0 or any negative number is a usage error: nothing is written to stdout, a non-empty usage/error message is written to stderr, and the exit status is 2. Either main() returning 2 or raising SystemExit(2) (as argparse does via parser.error) is acceptable; the tests accept both. The standard-library argparse module is the expected approach; no new dependency. Change only src/samplecli/cli.py. greet() in src/samplecli/greet.py stays byte-for-byte unchanged. Do not change main()'s signature or edit tests; tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_cli_blank_name.py and tests/test_cli_collapse_whitespace.py must still pass. Risk: medium, not high. The change adds a public CLI flag (a public_api-style change), but this manifest's owner_approval.required_for lists only new_dependency, and no dependency is added. It is rounded up from the manifest's low because it changes the CLI's public argument surface.

criteria.text: main(['--repeat', '3', 'Ada']) exits 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, Ada!\n' three times
the option may follow the name: main(['Ada', '--repeat', '2']) exits 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, Ada!\n' twice
--repeat 1 prints exactly one line: main(['--repeat', '1', 'Ada']) prints 'Hello, Ada!\n'
name normalisation still applies with --repeat: main(['--repeat', '2', '  Ada   Lovelace\t']) prints exactly 'Hello, Ada Lovelace!\n' twice
with --repeat and no name the greeting uses 'world': main(['--repeat', '2']) prints exactly 'Hello, world!\n' twice
without --repeat the greeting prints once: main(['Ada']) exits 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, Ada!\n'
--repeat 0, -1 or -5 is a usage error: exit status 2 (returned or raised as SystemExit), empty stdout, non-empty stderr

out_of_scope: changing the greet-003 strip/'world' fallback or greet-005 whitespace-collapse behaviour
other CLI flags, short aliases (-r, -n) or help-text wording
behaviour for non-integer N beyond whatever argparse type=int does
third-party argument parsing libraries, packaging and pyproject.toml
